summary.text: David Jolly, a Democrat who represented Florida's 13th District in Congress as a Republican from 2014 to 2017, lost the November 3, 2026 election for governor of Florida to Byron Donalds.
He left the Republican Party in 2018, joined the Democratic Party in 2025, and ran with former U.S. Rep. Gwen Graham.

His platform included a state catastrophic-risk fund for property insurance, Medicaid expansion, a moratorium on hyperscale data centers, campaign-finance and ethics reform, and codifying the Roe/Casey abortion framework in Florida law.

paragraphs.text: Jolly earned a B.A. from Emory University in 1994 and a J.D. from George Mason University School of Law in 2001.
He was a staff member for Rep. Bill Young from 1994 to 2006.
Jolly represented Florida's 13th Congressional District in the U.S. House as a Republican from March 14, 2014, to January 3, 2017.
He later served as an independent from 2018 to 2022, was a member of the Forward Party from 2022 to 2025, and has been a Democrat since 2025.
In 2022 he announced the formation of the Forward Party with Andrew Yang and Christine Todd Whitman.
Jolly is an attorney who served for nearly a decade as a political analyst on NBC and MSNBC.
He and his wife are raising their family in Pinellas County.
He received 48.7% of the vote to Byron Donalds's 50%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
